solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Mark learnt about making wrapping for goods

indicators.note: the reversed word is said to wrap round the goods, so they go inside it
about tells us to turn the word for learnt round, reading it backwards

parts.note: learnt means read, as in having read up on a subject
G is short for good, so goods doubles it to two Gs

explanation.surface: A student's grade is noted while they learn about how to pack merchandise.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Mark' looks like a grade or a verb, but it is the printer's symbol. Plural 'goods' as two G's is a typical Toughie liberty.
explanation.definitionFit: A dagger is the printer's obelus, a typographical mark used for footnotes.

clue.text: Drink Bermuda rum touring island

indicators.note: touring says the rearranged letters go round the island letter
rum means odd or strange, so the word Bermuda is put into a strange order

explanation.surface: A rum cocktail from Bermuda served while visiting an island.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rum' looks like the drink but is the anagram signal meaning odd.
explanation.definitionFit: Drambuie is a Scotch whisky liqueur flavoured with honey and herbs.

clue.text: Legal skit involved old statesman

indicators.note: involved suggests the letters are tangled together into a new order

explanation.surface: A courtroom sketch featured a retired politician.
explanation.definitionFit: Hugh Gaitskell led Britain's Labour Party from 1955 until his death in 1963.

clue.text: Fast runner departed match

parts.note: the emu is a large flightless bird that runs very fast
the late, meaning dead, have departed

explanation.surface: A sprinter quit the fixture.
explanation.walkthrough: 'match' reads as a sporting fixture but is the verb: to equal.
explanation.definitionFit: To emulate someone is to try to equal or rival them, to match their achievements.

clue.text: Occasional copies I'd reviewed

indicators.note: reviewed suggests the words have been gone over and reworked into a new order

explanation.surface: Duplicates I've looked over turn up only now and then.
explanation.definitionFit: Something episodic happens in separate, irregular episodes rather than continuously, so it is occasional.

clue.text: Wolves, given time, break deal made by agent

parts.note: wolves hunt in a pack
an age is a period of time
a holiday is a break from work

explanation.surface: Wolverhampton Wanderers, given time, wreck a transfer an agent negotiated.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Wolves' is the nickname of Wolverhampton Wanderers football club, fitting the agent's transfer deal.
explanation.definitionFit: A travel agent sells an all-in trip bundling flights and hotel as one deal.

clue.text: Maybe cook gravlax, evenly getting dispatched round

indicators.note: round says the dispatched word goes round the picked letters

parts.note: dispatched means sent off

indicators.note: evenly picks out the even-numbered letters of the word

explanation.surface: A chef sends out cured salmon, plated neatly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'evenly' picks R, V and A, the 2nd, 4th and 6th letters of 'gravlax'.
explanation.definitionFit: A cook in a household is one example of a domestic servant.

clue.text: Play around, ultimately before God

indicators.note: before places the picked letter ahead of the god in this down entry
ultimately picks the very last letter of the word

parts.note: Rama is a Hindu god, an avatar of Vishnu

explanation.surface: Fooling about at the last, then standing before the Almighty.
explanation.definitionFit: A drama is a play for stage, screen or radio.

clue.text: Emperor waves back when chauffeured?

indicators.note: when chauffeured, the reversed waves are carried inside the vehicle

parts.note: being chauffeured means riding in a car

indicators.note: back says the word for waves is read in reverse

parts.note: the sea is made of waves

explanation.surface: A ruler waves back at the crowd while being driven past.
explanation.walkthrough: 'waves back' reads as a royal greeting, but the waves are the sea, read in reverse.
explanation.definitionFit: Caesar became the title of Roman emperors after Julius Caesar.

clue.text: The establishment irritated Smiley, having left out insurgent

indicators.note: irritated suggests the letters are stirred up and thrown into a new order
out, with having, says the next letter is dropped from Smiley

explanation.surface: John le Carré's spymaster Smiley was annoyed to have missed a rebel.
explanation.walkthrough: 'having left out' removes L from SMILEY, giving SMIEY; 'irritated' mixes those letters with INSURGENT.
explanation.definitionFit: Men in grey suits are the faceless senior figures who wield power behind the scenes, the Establishment.

clue.text: Gold rings break for so long

indicators.note: the gold symbol rings, or encircles, the next word

parts.note: AU is the chemical symbol for gold
to break down, as an engine does, is to die

explanation.surface: Gold wedding bands fall apart, so that's goodbye to them.
explanation.definitionFit: Both are farewells: so long is an informal goodbye, and the French word means the same.

clue.text: Roast ox with rice cooked and consumed

indicators.note: cooked suggests the ingredients ox and rice are mixed up into new letters

parts.note: consumed means ate, past tense of eat

explanation.surface: A recipe: ox roasted with rice, then eaten.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Roast' sits in the kitchen picture as cooking, but here it means to criticise savagely.
explanation.definitionFit: To roast someone is to criticise them severely, and to excoriate is to censure harshly.

clue.text: It's dull splitting mostly plain type of rice

indicators.note: splitting says the dull word goes into the middle of the other, cutting it open
mostly says the word for plain loses its final letter

parts.note: plain means basic, simple and unadorned
matt or mat means dull, without a shine

explanation.surface: Something dull cuts through an ordinary sort of rice.
explanation.definitionFit: Basmati is a long-grain rice variety from South Asia, often served with curry.

clue.text: Seaman entertained by a priest in Gulf state?

indicators.note: entertained by puts the seaman inside, as a guest is within a host's house

parts.note: a lama is a Tibetan Buddhist priest
AB stands for able-bodied seaman

explanation.surface: A sailor is hosted by a holy man somewhere on the Persian Gulf.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Gulf state' suggests the Middle East, but the gulf is the Gulf of Mexico, hence the question mark.
explanation.definitionFit: Alabama is a US state with a coastline on the Gulf of Mexico.

clue.text: Leaves cubicle, teetering, but not in pants

indicators.note: pants is British slang for rubbish, so the letters are a mess to be rearranged
but not says the following word is removed from teetering

explanation.surface: Someone leaves a changing cubicle wobbling, though not wearing trousers.
explanation.walkthrough: 'but not in' removes IN from TEETERING, leaving TEETERG; 'pants' then mixes that with CUBICLE.
explanation.definitionFit: This crisp lettuce is eaten as salad leaves.

clue.text: Cheat put instrument below deck?

indicators.note: below puts the instrument under the cards in this down entry

parts.note: a deck is a pack of playing cards
the harp is a stringed instrument

explanation.surface: A trickster stowed a musical instrument below a ship's deck.
explanation.walkthrough: 'deck' suggests a ship, but it is a pack of cards.
explanation.definitionFit: A cardsharp is a cheat who wins at cards by sleight of hand.

clue.text: Slip up about occupants of house getting support

indicators.note: about says the reversed word goes round the house's inner letters
up reads the slip word backwards in this down entry

parts.note: a slip is a lapse, a small error

indicators.note: the occupants are the middle letters, those inside the house

explanation.surface: A mistake about the residents of a home attracts backing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'support' here is a noun, the act of backing a cause, not a physical prop.
explanation.definitionFit: Espousal of a cause is the adoption or championing of it, giving it support.

clue.text: Dressing by churchgoers briefly cast in this?

parts.note: a plaster is a sticking dressing for a cut
of can mean by, as in the works of an author

indicators.note: briefly cuts off the last letter

parts.note: a parish is the congregation of a church

explanation.surface: A wound dressing beside the congregation, perhaps a broken limb set in it.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition leans on the whole clue: the dressing material is what a cast is made of.
explanation.definitionFit: Plaster casts for broken bones are made from this gypsum powder mixed with water.

clue.text: Spotted that man with bit on the side entering dodgy boozer

indicators.note: entering says the man and bit go inside the spotted word

parts.note: spotted means seen
he refers to that man
B is the abbreviation for a bit in computing

explanation.surface: A man was seen with his mistress going into a seedy pub.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bit on the side' suggests a lover, but only 'bit' gives B; 'on the side' joins.
explanation.definitionFit: A shebeen, chiefly Irish or South African, is an unlicensed drinking den, so an illicit pub.

clue.text: Spotted feline quietly sitting on part of plant

indicators.note: sitting on puts the quiet letter above the plant part in this down entry

parts.note: P, piano, is the musical instruction for quietly
the anther is the pollen-bearing part of a flower's stamen

explanation.surface: A leopard silently sits on a flower.
explanation.definitionFit: Panther is another name for the leopard, a big cat with a spotted coat.

clue.text: Friend climbing cairn, perhaps one that's walked all over?

indicators.note: climbing reads the friend word upwards, backwards in this down entry

parts.note: a pal is a friend
a cairn terrier is a small breed of dog

explanation.surface: A mate scales a pile of stones that hikers traipse across.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cairn' looks like a hill marker of stones, but it is a terrier.
explanation.definitionFit: A lapdog is a fawning, subservient person whom others treat as a doormat, and the pet is literally walked.

clue.text: Discoveries, say, framing core element of systems software

indicators.note: framing says the apples go round the core letter

parts.note: Discovery is an English apple variety, so Discoveries are examples of apples

indicators.note: the core element is the central letter of the word

explanation.surface: Findings surround the key part of computer systems' programs.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Discoveries' reads as findings, but it is the apple variety; the capital hides it at the start.
explanation.definitionFit: Applets are small application programs, a kind of software, often run in a browser.

clue.text: Dance masks intermittently cut up

indicators.note: up reverses the whole construction in this down entry
intermittently takes every other letter of the word

parts.note: to lop is to cut off

explanation.surface: At a masked ball, the masks are slashed now and then.
explanation.walkthrough: 'intermittently' picks A and K from 'masks'; AK plus LOP, read upwards, gives the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: The polka is a lively Bohemian couple dance in two-four time.

clue.text: Current company binding stories for old dramatist

indicators.note: binding says the current and company letters wrap round the stories

parts.note: I is the symbol for electric current
ones are stories or jokes, as in 'have you heard the one about...'

explanation.surface: A modern firm publishes a collection of tales by a playwright of old.
explanation.definitionFit: Eugène Ionesco was a Romanian-French playwright of the Theatre of the Absurd, who died in 1994.

clue.text: Fool backing famous musical secures life of luxury

indicators.note: backing says the word for fool is read backwards

parts.note: a clod is a dull, foolish person
Evita is the Lloyd Webber musical about Eva Perón

explanation.surface: An idiot invests in a hit show and gains a lavish lifestyle.
explanation.definitionFit: The Italian phrase means 'sweet life', a life of pleasure and luxury.

clue.text: Lead shot's opening floating can?

parts.note: to head something is to lead it

indicators.note: opening picks the first letter of the word

explanation.surface: The start of a lead pellet's flight is like a bobbing tin.
explanation.walkthrough: 'can' is slang for a toilet, and 'floating' puts it on a ship.
explanation.definitionFit: On a ship the toilets are called the heads, so they are a seaborne lavatory.

clue.text: Open policy number retained by young woman in sporty car

indicators.note: in says the whole lot sits inside the car

parts.note: GT, gran turismo, labels a sporty car

indicators.note: retained by says the number is held inside the young woman

parts.note: a lass is a girl or young woman

explanation.surface: A girl in a sports car keeps quiet about a figure, yet follows a policy of openness.
explanation.definitionFit: Glasnost was Gorbachev's Soviet policy of openness and transparency in government.

clue.text: Finally change hands in correct move

indicators.note: the final letter swaps from right hand to left hand, R to L

parts.note: correct means proper, as in proper behaviour

explanation.surface: A chess or card player switches hands at the end to make the right move.
explanation.definitionFit: To propel something is to drive or push it forward, to move it.
